name: Touch
overview: The Bible presents touch as a powerful and significant act that can convey both holiness and healing. In the Old Testament, God forbids touching certain things to prevent death or defilement, such as the forbidden fruit in Genesis 3:3 and unclean conditions in Leviticus 12:4, while also commanding protection for His anointed through the injunction in Psalms 105:15. In the New Testament, Jesus demonstrates the compassionate and restorative nature of touch by healing the sick and encouraging faith, as seen in Matthew 9:29, Matthew 17:7, and Mark 1:41. Thus, Scripture reveals touch as an expression of divine authority, sanctity, and grace.
